subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.explain: Abstract Expressionism used large-scale, energetic, often non-figurative gestural marks.

questions.q: Salvador Dali is associated with which art movement?
questions.explain: Salvador Dali was a leading Surrealist, known for dream-like works such as his melting clocks.

options: Capturing fleeting light and everyday scenes with loose brushwork
questions.explain: Impressionists used loose, visible brushstrokes to capture changing light and ordinary moments.

questions.q: Cubism is most associated with which two artists?
questions.explain: Cubism was pioneered by Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque in the early 20th century.

questions.q: Which artist is most associated with Pop Art and images of soup cans?
questions.explain: Andy Warhol was a leading Pop Art figure, famous for his Campbell's soup can images.

questions.q: When analysing an artwork, which is the best opening focus?
options: How long it took to frame
What you can see and how the formal elements are used
questions.explain: Good analysis starts by describing what you see and how line, colour, tone and composition are used.

questions.q: Which assessment objective involves responding to the work of other artists?
options: Developing ideas through investigation of sources
questions.explain: Developing ideas requires investigating sources, including the work of relevant artists and cultures.

options: The dream world and the unconscious mind
questions.explain: Surrealism drew on dreams and the unconscious to create strange, irrational imagery.

options: Be unrelated to your earlier work
Bring together your research and development into your own resolved piece
questions.explain: A personal response resolves your investigations and development into your own meaningful final outcome.

questions.q: Which artist is closely linked to Impressionism?
questions.explain: Claude Monet was a founder of Impressionism, famous for paintings such as his water lilies.

questions.q: What is the purpose of 'annotation' in a sketchbook?
options: To explain your thinking, choices and development in words
To list the cost of materials
To fill empty space with decoration
questions.explain: Annotation uses written notes to explain your ideas, decisions and how your work is developing.

questions.q: Jackson Pollock is famous for which technique?
options: Dripping and pouring paint onto canvas
questions.explain: Jackson Pollock developed a 'drip' technique, pouring paint onto canvas laid on the floor.
